z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                if (x == 0 || x == nx-1 || y == 0 || y == ny-1 || z == 0 || z == nz-1) {\n                    const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                    output[idx] = input[idx];\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<Real>& grid, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    // Simple sanity checks\n    \n    // 1. No NaN or Inf values\n    for (const auto& val : grid) {\n        if (std::isnan(val) || std::isinf(val)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // 2. Now I'm working out the original program's behavior: it parses command-line flags for dimensions and iteration counts, initializes the grid using a modulo pattern based on global index, then runs the specified number of stencil iterations.\n\nTracking the double-buffering logic carefully — even iterations read/write differently than odd, and I need to watch edge cases like zero or negative iteration counts where buffers might end up uninitialized or zeroed. Boundaries only get copied during the stencil step, and crucially, the final statistics (sum via Kahan summation, min/max, and an FNV hash) are all order-dependent, which means I must gather the final grid to rank 0 in the exact global ordering to reproduce identical output.\n\nI'm reasoning through floating-point determinism: since the stencil computation is pure addition followed by division by 7.0 with no multiplication, FMA contraction isn't a concern on either CPU or GPU, and I need to make sure nvcc isn't using fast-math so division stays IEEE-compliant. I also need to preserve the global index used in initialization and decide whether to gather the full grid to rank 0 for validation or do a distributed reduction instead.\n\nFor the hybrid design, I'm settling on a slab decomposition along the z-axis since the layout is z-major, making halo exchanges simple contiguous plane copies that work well for both CPU and GPU, though I'm weighing whether a full 3D decomposition would be needed for better scalability with many ranks.\n\nFor GPU assignment, each rank uses MPI_Comm_split_type with MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED to find its local rank, then picks a device via local rank modulo device count, keeping data resident on the GPU across iterations and exchanging halo planes by copying the contiguous boundary plane to pinned host buffers for MPI_Sendrecv rather than relying on CUDA-aware MPI.\n\nTo overlap communication with compute, I want each iteration to first compute the boundary z-planes on the GPU, then kick off asynchronous device-to-host copies of those planes while the interior planes are computed, followed by MPI exchange and host-to-device copies into the halo slots, with fixed global boundaries just copied through rather than averaged.\n\nSo for rank 0, which owns global planes starting at z=0, that boundary plane is included directly rather than through a halo. Each rank owns global planes [z0, z1), with local index zl mapping to gz - z0 + 1 to account for the halo offset.\n\nNow I need to figure out how planes are distributed across ranks — dividing nz planes evenly as z0 = floor(r*nz/P). The tricky part is when there are more ranks than planes, leaving some ranks with zero owned planes, which complicates halo exchange logic; I'm leaning toward just requiring nz >= size and erroring out otherwise, though that changes behavior compared to the reference.\n\nActually no communicator split is needed — I can just use MPI_PROC_NULL for neighbor ranks beyond the active range, letting inactive ranks skip the stencil work entirely and simply join the final gather. Edge cases like nz<=2 still work fine since the interior loop naturally becomes empty while boundary copies remain valid.\n\nNow I'm sketching the CUDA halo-exchange pipeline: using ping-pong device buffers sized for local z-planes plus halos, computing boundary planes first on one stream, copying those boundary results device-to-host for the MPI exchange, while concurrently launching the interior-plane kernel on a separate compute stream to overlap communication with computation.\n\nOn sBoundary I'm async copying the two boundary planes D2H into pinned memory and recording an event when that's done. Meanwhile the interior kernel launches on sInterior independently since those planes only depend on data already local, not on the halo exchange.\n\nOn the host side, I sync on the boundary-copy event, do the MPI_Sendrecv exchange via pinned buffers, then issue the H2D copy of the received halos back on sBoundary, relying on stream ordering so the next iteration's kernels on that stream naturally wait for the fresh halo data before using it.\n\nTracing through the double-buffer dependency carefully: the interior kernel only touches planes 1 through nzl of its input, never the halo planes, while the boundary kernel for the edge planes does need the halos and runs on sBoundary right after the H2D copy, so ordering holds. Checking across iterations too — each iteration swaps input/output buffers, and since the writes to the new buffer (interior on sInterior, edges on sBoundary) don't overlap the untouched old buffer's halo copies, there's no race between consecutive iterations as long as the streams preserve this ordering.\n\nMaybe a simpler approach is better: just synchronize both streams at the end of each iteration, sacrificing cross-iteration overlap. Within a single iteration, the boundary kernel, D2H copy, and MPI exchange can still overlap with the big interior kernel, which is where most of the compute cost lives anyway.\n\nSo the ordering on sBoundary is: boundary kernel runs, then D2H copies for lo and hi halos, then the host syncs on sBoundary, does the MPI exchange, and finally issues the H2D copies into the output halos asynchronously on that same stream, while interior kernel keeps running independently on sInterior during the host's wait.\n\nI want to launch the boundary kernel before the interior kernel so the small boundary work (just 1-2 planes) isn't delayed, letting both streams execute concurrently on the device. The boundary kernel just needs a plane-count parameter to handle either one or two boundary planes depending on local z-extent, with the interior kernel covering whatever planes remain in between, and the global domain edges naturally fall out of the same copy condition in the kernel.\n\nFor thread mapping I'm using a 3D grid where each block handles a tile in x/y and the z dimension maps directly to local plane index, keeping memory access coalesced along x. Indices are computed with 64-bit types to avoid overflow, with local offsets accounting for the halo plane at the front, and initialization mirrors the original hash-based approach but using the rank's global z offset so each plane gets the same values as the monolithic version.\n\nFor out-of-range halo planes (before z=0 or after z=nz-1) I just set them to 0 since those values never get read, which means no initial halo exchange is needed before the first iteration starts. I still need to handle edge cases around the iteration count parity -- matching what the original does when iterations is zero or negative so the final buffer selection (grid1 vs grid2) stays consistent, including the negative case where grid2 would just be zeros.\n\nFor timing, I'll match the original's approach of only measuring the iteration loop itself, adding an MPI barrier before starting the clock and a device sync after the loop to keep the GPU measurement accurate.\n\nPrints should only happen on rank 0 to match the original's output exactly, and I'll only gather the full grid to rank 0 when validation or result-printing flags are set, since otherwise it's wasted work. For gathering, since each rank's local buffer stores its owned z-planes contiguously and ranks are ordered by z-range, I can use MPI_Gatherv with counts and displacements computed directly from each rank's slab size and starting offset.\n\nI need a host staging buffer to copy device data into before gathering, and rank 0 needs the full-size vector to receive into; pageable host memory is fine here since gather is only used for final output, not performance-critical paths. For device assignment, I'll split the communicator by shared memory type to find the local rank within a node, then use that to assign GPUs round-robin via cudaSetDevice.\n\nI'm thinking about where OpenMP fits in — probably for host-side work like parallel initialization, validation scans with reductions, and possibly a hybrid CPU+GPU split where OpenMP threads compute part of the slab concurrently with the GPU, while keeping the Kahan summation and hashing sequential to preserve correctness.\n\nInitialization can legitimately use OpenMP too: generate the initial slab and halos on the host in parallel, then copy to device, since timing excludes init. I could also parallelize the NaN/min/max validation scan with an OpenMP reduction, since min/max are exact and reproducible — that's a clean, honest use of threads beyond just init.\n\nFor the rest: the hash printing in print_results stays sequential, multi-GPU just relies on one MPI rank per GPU naturally, and hybrid CPU+GPU compute isn't worth the complexity so I'll skip it and just mention it as a tradeoff. For single-rank runs, MPI_PROC_NULL sendrecvs are no-ops, so I'll skip the halo H2D copy entirely when there's no neighbor rather than copying harmless garbage. Finally, the CMakeLists needs to declare both CXX and CUDA as project languages to avoid nvcc/-march=native conflicts.\n\nFor GPU architecture targeting, I'm setting CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES to cover a broad range of compute capabilities (70 through 90) so the RTX 3090's sm_86 is included without requiring CMake 3.24's \"native\" detection, keeping it compatible with a wider range of CMake versions.\n\nSince I can't create new files, the CUDA code has to live inside stencil3d.cpp, compiled as CUDA via setting its source file language property so nvcc processes it. I'm worried nvcc (CUDA 12.0) might reject GCC 13 as an unsupported host compiler for C++20 — I'll need to test this, and if it fails, consider the `-allow-unsupported-compiler` workaround as a fallback.\n\nI also need to pass -march=native and -Wall through -Xcompiler for nvcc, and figure out how CMake handles OpenMP flags for CUDA-language sources, since nvcc likely rejects -fopenmp directly and needs it wrapped as -Xcompiler=-fopenmp via explicit compile-language generator expressions.\n\nI'm also checking that MPI include paths flow correctly into nvcc through the CMake MPI::MPI_CXX target, and confirming that the 7-point stencil sum keeps a fixed left-to-right addition order with plain IEEE division so GPU and CPU results stay bit-consistent without fast-math reassociation.\n\nI plan to verify this by saving a copy of the original source to a scratch directory and diffing outputs across multiple ranks and configurations. Now I'm sketching the stencil kernel itself, computing a per-plane 2D thread grid where each block handles one z-plane offset from a given start index, with x and y positions derived from block and thread indices.\n\nI'm working out the indexing carefully: converting local plane index to global z, checking boundary conditions on all six faces (x, y, and z edges), and for interior points summing the center plus six neighbors in the same order as the original (left, right, front, back, bottom, top) divided by seven, while being careful about edge cases like nx=1 matching the original's loop bounds exactly.\n\nI decide not to bother supporting nx=0 since the original also breaks down there, and plan the launch strategy: skip empty z-ranges, split boundary planes at zl=1 and zl=nzl, and handle the interior range separately when nzl>2. For performance I'm considering whether the simple 7-load stencil kernel relies enough on L2 caching for neighbor reuse, or whether a tiled shared-memory approach would meaningfully reduce memory traffic.\n\nI settle on keeping the 32x4 thread block simple since plane sizes fit comfortably within the RTX 3090's L2 cache, so the straightforward kernel should perform well without z-sliding tricks. For halo exchange, I'm setting up pinned host buffers sized to a single plane and working out the MPI_Sendrecv pairing so each rank's top owned plane becomes its neighbor's bottom halo and vice versa.\n\nI need to make sure the send/receive tags between adjacent ranks match up correctly so the lo-plane send from one rank lines up with the hi-plane receive on the neighboring rank, so I'm using distinct tags to avoid any ambiguity in the exchange pattern.\n\nI think switching to Isend/Irecv with four requests and a single Waitall is simpler and avoids any deadlock concerns from ordering, and pinned host memory should work fine without needing CUDA-aware MPI. MPI_Init is fine since only the main thread calls MPI while OpenMP handles host-side initialization.\n\nChecking the overlap timing: boundary exchange latency is a few hundred microseconds per iteration against roughly 0.1-0.3ms of interior GPU work for a 128³ grid, so overlapping the interior kernel with the halo exchange is worthwhile and scaling up to larger grids is the real target. For memory, doubling the device buffers for something like 1024³ cells comes to about 16GB, which fits within a 24GB card like the RTX 3090, similar to what the original host-based allocation would need.\n\nFor initialization, I'm weighing host-side init with OpenMP followed by a copy to device versus a direct device kernel init — the device kernel avoids doubling memory and an extra transfer, but then OpenMP's role shrinks to mainly the validation scan on rank 0, so I want to be honest that OpenMP is used specifically there while init and halo exchange rely on CUDA and MPI respectively.\n\nFor validation, I can keep the existing validateResult logic but add OpenMP reductions for the NaN check and min/max computation since those produce identical numerical results while parallelizing the scan over the full grid, which matters for something like a 1024^3 domain. The sequential hash print in print_results stays untouched since correctness there depends on order.\n\nThinking more about architecture, I consider whether a true hybrid MPI+OpenMP+CUDA design — one rank per node with OpenMP threads each driving a GPU and handling intra-node halos through host memory — would give OpenMP a more substantial role, but that adds real complexity versus the simpler, robust rank-per-GPU approach that already performs well via MPI's shared-memory optimizations. I'll stick with rank-per-GPU and use OpenMP for host-side loops like validation, while being honest that OpenMP's role here is limited rather than central to performance.\n\nFor the final gather, I'm planning to copy each rank's owned slab from device to host and combine them with Gatherv, letting rank 0 use MPI_IN_PLACE since its data already sits at the start of the full host buffer. I also need to handle the edge case where some ranks own zero planes if the process count exceeds the number of z-slices, making sure their counts are set to zero correctly in the gather call.\n\nWorking through the decomposition more carefully, I'm limiting active ranks to min(P, nz) and distributing z-planes evenly among them, with inactive ranks getting zero planes. Neighbor computation needs PROC_NULL for the boundary between the last active rank and the first inactive one, and inactive ranks still need to participate in barriers for timing even though they skip GPU allocation and halo exchange work.\n\nFor the edge case where a rank owns just a single z-plane, the same plane serves as both its low and high boundary for exchange purposes, so the send/receive logic naturally handles it by copying that one plane twice. I'm making sure the initialization kernel computes global indices consistently across local and halo regions so neighboring planes agree on values, filling the whole slab (including halo space) using the same formula when the global z-index is valid, and zeroing out anything outside the real domain or in the output buffer.\n\nFor the final result selection when iterations is zero or negative, I pick between grid1 or grid2 based on the parity of iterations, matching the original logic exactly. For timing, I sync each rank's GPU work before an MPI barrier, then measure elapsed time across ranks — since the barrier forces all ranks to finish before timing stops, this should effectively capture the max time across ranks like the original single-loop timing.\n\nNow I'm structuring the per-iteration loop: picking which buffer is input versus output based on iteration parity, launching boundary stencil kernels first, kicking off async device-to-host copies of boundary results into send buffers, then launching the interior kernel while those copies happen, followed by waiting on the boundary stream, exchanging halo data via non-blocking MPI sends/receives, and finally copying received halo data back into the device buffers...\n\nI note that using PROC_NULL for missing neighbors lets the same four-request pattern work uniformly, since MPI completes those immediately, and I'm confirming the interior kernel can run concurrently on its own stream while the boundary exchange proceeds on another.\n\nFor the final gather, I'm having each rank copy its owned planes into a host buffer, but rank 0 writes directly into its slot of the full output vector to avoid an extra copy before calling MPI_Gatherv.\n\nOne thing I need to watch: MPI_Gatherv counts are ints, and for very large grids (nzl*nx*ny) the per-rank count could overflow 32-bit, so I should check whether the original design already accounts for that size limit.\n\nRank 0 handles gathering the full grid when printing or validation is needed, then calls validateResult on the assembled data and prints results through print_results, keeping all output restricted to the root process while other ranks stay silent.\n\nFor argument parsing, all ranks need to process the same arguments consistently after MPI_Init so every process reaches MPI_Finalize together -- rank 0 handles any usage/error messages for -h or unknown options, but all ranks must still exit together to avoid hangs. I need to make sure the exit code from validation failures (normally returning 1) is properly reflected even though only rank 0 holds the actual data, since other ranks would otherwise default to a mismatched success code.\n\nFor GPU setup, I'm having each process check its CUDA device count and abort via MPI_Abort if none are found, then assign devices to local ranks using a communicator split by node for oversubscription handling. For the validation logic, I want to preserve the original order of checks -- first scan for NaN/Inf values using an OpenMP reduction, print an error and bail if found, then compute and print the min/max value range only if the data passed that first check.\n\nI'm also considering a subtle edge case around negative zero in min/max reductions, but since all grid values are non-negative, this shouldn't matter in practice. Now I'll write the hybrid version. The design:\n\n- **MPI**: 1D slab decomposition along z across ranks. Each rank owns a contiguous range of z-planes plus one halo plane on each side. Halo planes are contiguous in memory, so no packing is needed.\n- **CUDA**: each rank binds to one GPU (by node-local rank). The grid lives on the device across all iterations. Boundary planes are computed first on a high-priority stream, copied to pinned host buffers, and exchanged over MPI while the interior kernel runs on a second stream.\n- **OpenMP**: used for the host-side validation scan on rank 0 (NaN/Inf check and min/max reductions). {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793098032792,"sessionID":"ses_e830aaf12ffeLU1hMxNQW9to5S","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01HmG2d8SkbpZ8HkAdeXzpNa","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/stencil3d_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA 3D 7-point stencil benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   * MPI:    1D slab decomposition along Z. Each rank owns a contiguous range\n//             of Z-planes and exchanges one halo plane with each neighbour per\n//             iteration. Z-planes are contiguous in memory, so halos need no\n//             packing.\n//   * CUDA:   each rank binds to one GPU (chosen by node-local rank). The grid\n//             stays resident on the device for all iterations. Per iteration the\n//             boundary planes are computed first on a high-priority stream and\n//             copied to pinned host buffers; the halo exchange then overlaps with\n//             the interior-plane kernel running on a second stream.\n//   * OpenMP: host-side validation scans (NaN/Inf check, min/max) on rank 0.\n//\n// The per-cell arithmetic and its evaluation order are identical to the serial\n// reference, so results (including the printed hash/sum) are bit-identical.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nusing Real = double;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                 \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                       \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                       \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,             \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                           \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                \\\n        }                                                                                \\\n    } while (0)\n\n#define ROOT_PRINTF(...)                                                                 \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        if (rank == 0) printf(__VA_ARGS__);                                              \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Initial grid value for a local element. zl is the local plane index (0 is the\n// lower halo plane, zl = nzl+1 is the upper halo plane); z0 is the global Z of the\n// first owned plane. Halo planes outside the global domain are zero (never read).\n__global__ void initKernel(Real* __restrict__ grid, const size_t nx, const size_t ny,\n                           const size_t nz, const size_t z0, const size_t localElems) {\n    const size_t nxy = nx * ny;\n    const size_t stride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x;\n    for (size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; i < localElems; i += stride) {\n        const size_t zl = i / nxy;\n        const size_t rem = i - zl * nxy;\n        const long long gz = static_cast<long long>(z0) + static_cast<long long>(zl) - 1;\n        if (gz < 0 || gz >= static_cast<long long>(nz)) {\n            grid[i] = 0.0;\n        } else {\n            const size_t gidx = static_cast<size_t>(gz) * nxy + rem;  // == idx3(x, y, gz, nx, ny)\n            grid[i] = static_cast<Real>(gidx % 19) * 1.0;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// 7-point stencil over local planes [zlFirst, zlFirst + zCount).\n// Global boundary cells are copied; all other cells are averaged.\n__global__ void stencilKernel(const Real* __restrict__ in, Real* __restrict__ out,\n                              const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz, const size_t z0,\n                              const size_t zlFirst, const size_t zCount) {\n    const size_t nxy = nx * ny;\n    const size_t x = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (x >= nx) return;\n    const size_t yStride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.y) * blockDim.y;\n    for (size_t zi = blockIdx.z; zi < zCount; zi += gridDim.z) {\n        const size_t zl = zlFirst + zi;\n        const size_t gz = z0 + zl - 1;\n        const bool zBoundary = (gz == 0) || (gz == nz - 1);\n        for (size_t y = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y; y < ny; y += yStride) {\n            const size_t idx = zl * nxy + y * nx + x;\n            if (zBoundary || x == 0 || x == nx - 1 || y == 0 || y == ny - 1) {\n                out[idx] = in[idx];\n                continue;\n            }\n            const Real center = in[idx];\n            const Real left = in[idx - 1];\n            const Real right = in[idx + 1];\n            const Real front = in[idx - nx];\n            const Real back = in[idx + nx];\n            const Real bottom = in[idx - nxy];\n            const Real top = in[idx + nxy];\n            // Simple averaging stencil (same operation order as the reference)\n            out[idx] = (center + left + right + front + back + bottom + top) / 7.0;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic void launchStencil(cudaStream_t stream, const Real* in, Real* out, const size_t nx, const size_t ny,\n                          const size_t nz, const size_t z0, const size_t zlFirst, const size_t zCount) {\n    if (zCount == 0 || nx == 0 || ny == 0) return;\n    const dim3 block(32, 4, 1);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned>((nx + block.x - 1) / block.x),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>(std::min<size_t>((ny + block.y - 1) / block.y, 65535)),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>(std::min<size_t>(zCount, 65535)));\n    stencilKernel<<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(in, out, nx, ny, nz, z0, zlFirst, zCount);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<Real>& grid, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    const long long n = static_cast<long long>(grid.size());\n\n    // 1. No NaN or Inf values\n    bool hasNonFinite = false;\n#pragma omp parallel for reduction(|| : hasNonFinite)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        hasNonFinite = hasNonFinite || std::isnan(grid[i]) || std::isinf(grid[i]);\n    }\n    if (hasNonFinite) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // 2. Values should be reasonable (bounded)\n    Real minVal = grid[0];\n    Real maxVal = grid[0];\n#pragma omp parallel for reduction(min : minVal) reduction(max : maxVal)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, grid[i]);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, grid[i]);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Value range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n\n    // After averaging, values should be somewhat bounded\n    if (maxVal > 1e6 || minVal < -1e6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Boundary values should not change significantly\n    // (they are copied, so they should be close to initial values)\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 128)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n// Z-slab owned by rank r when `nActive` ranks share `nz` planes.\nstruct Slab {\n    size_t z0;\n    size_t nzl;\n};\n\nstatic Slab slabFor(const int r, const int nActive, const size_t nz) {\n    if (r >= nActive) return {nz, 0};\n    const size_t a = static_cast<size_t>(r) * nz / nActive;\n    const size_t b = static_cast<size_t>(r + 1) * nz / nActive;\n    return {a, b - a};\n}\n\nstatic int runBenchmark(int argc, char** argv, const int rank, const int size) {\n    size_t nx = 128;\n    size_t ny = 0;  // Will be set to nx if not specified\n    size_t nz = 0;  // Will be set to nx if not specified\n    int iterations = 10;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"3D Stencil Benchmark\\n\");\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Iterations: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    const size_t nxy = nx * ny;\n    const size_t gridSize = nxy * nz;\n    if (nxy > static_cast<size_t>(INT_MAX)) {\n        if (rank == 0) fprintf(stderr, \"Plane size nx*ny exceeds supported limit\\n\");\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    const size_t planeBytes = nxy * sizeof(Real);\n\n    // --- Bind this rank to a GPU (round-robin over node-local ranks) ---\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount));\n    if (deviceCount == 0) {\n        if (rank == 0) fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA devices available\\n\");\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(localRank % deviceCount));\n\n    // --- Domain decomposition along Z ---\n    const int nActive = static_cast<int>(std::max<size_t>(1, std::min<size_t>(static_cast<size_t>(size), nz)));\n    const Slab mine = slabFor(rank, nActive, nz);\n    const size_t z0 = mine.z0;\n    const size_t nzl = mine.nzl;\n    const int upRank = (rank + 1 < nActive) ? rank + 1 : MPI_PROC_NULL;\n    const int downRank = (rank > 0 && rank < nActive) ? rank - 1 : MPI_PROC_NULL;\n\n    MPI_Datatype planeType;\n    MPI_Type_contiguous(static_cast<int>(nxy), MPI_DOUBLE, &planeType);\n    MPI_Type_commit(&planeType);\n\n    // --- Device / host resources ---\n    Real* d1 = nullptr;  // local grid (double buffer), layout: [halo | owned | halo]\n    Real* d2 = nullptr;\n    Real* hSendLo = nullptr;\n    Real* hSendHi = nullptr;\n    Real* hRecvLo = nullptr;\n    Real* hRecvHi = nullptr;\n\n    int leastPrio = 0, greatestPrio = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange(&leastPrio, &greatestPrio));\n    cudaStream_t sBnd, sInt;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(&sBnd, cudaStreamNonBlocking, greatestPrio));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(&sInt, cudaStreamNonBlocking, leastPrio));\n\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Initializing grid...\\n\");\n    if (nzl > 0) {\n        const size_t localElems = (nzl + 2) * nxy;\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d1, localElems * sizeof(Real)));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d2, localElems * sizeof(Real)));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemset(d2, 0, localElems * sizeof(Real)));\n\n        const int blocks = static_cast<int>(std::min<size_t>((localElems + 255) / 256, 65535));\n        initKernel<<<blocks, 256>>>(d1, nx, ny, nz, z0, localElems);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(&hSendLo, planeBytes));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(&hSendHi, planeBytes));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(&hRecvLo, planeBytes));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(&hRecvHi, planeBytes));\n    }\n\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Running stencil computation...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (int iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        if (nzl == 0) continue;  // Idle rank (more ranks than Z-planes)\n        const Real* in = (iter % 2 == 0) ? d1 : d2;\n        Real* out = (iter % 2 == 0) ? d2 : d1;\n\n        // 1) Boundary planes first (they feed the halo exchange).\n        launchStencil(sBnd, in, out, nx, ny, nz, z0, 1, 1);\n        if (nzl > 1) launchStencil(sBnd, in, out, nx, ny, nz, z0, nzl, 1);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(hSendLo, out + nxy, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, sBnd));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(hSendHi, out + nzl * nxy, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, sBnd));\n\n        // 2) Interior planes overlap with the halo exchange.\n        if (nzl > 2) launchStencil(sInt, in, out, nx, ny, nz, z0, 2, nzl - 2);\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(sBnd));\n\n        // 3) Halo exchange (tag 0: data moving up, tag 1: data moving down).\n        MPI_Request reqs[4];\n        MPI_Irecv(hRecvLo, 1, planeType, downRank, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &reqs[0]);\n        MPI_Irecv(hRecvHi, 1, planeType, upRank, 1, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &reqs[1]);\n        MPI_Isend(hSendHi, 1, planeType, upRank, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &reqs[2]);\n        MPI_Isend(hSendLo, 1, planeType, downRank, 1, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &reqs[3]);\n        MPI_Waitall(4, reqs, MPI_STATUSES_IGNORE);\n\n        // 4) Write received neighbour planes into the halo planes of 'out'.\n        if (downRank != MPI_PROC_NULL)\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(out, hRecvLo, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, sBnd));\n        if (upRank != MPI_PROC_NULL)\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(out + (nzl + 1) * nxy, hRecvHi, planeBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, sBnd));\n\n        // 5) Iteration barrier: 'out' must be complete before it becomes 'in'.\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(sBnd));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(sInt));\n    }\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    double cellUpdates = (double)((nx - 2) * (ny - 2) * (nz - 2)) * iterations;\n    double mcups = cellUpdates / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e6;  // Million cell updates per second\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Performance: %.3f MCellUpdates/s\\n\", mcups);\n\n    // Final grid lives in grid1 for an even iteration count, otherwise grid2.\n    const Real* finalDev = (iterations % 2 == 0) ? d1 : d2;\n    int rc = 0;\n\n    if (printResults || validate) {\n        // Gather the full final grid (global Z order) onto rank 0.\n        std::vector<Real> finalGrid;\n        std::vector<int> counts(size, 0), displs(size, 0);\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            const Slab s = slabFor(r, nActive, nz);\n            counts[r] = static_cast<int>(s.nzl);\n            displs[r] = static_cast<int>(s.z0);\n        }\n\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            finalGrid.resize(gridSize);\n            if (nzl > 0)\n                CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(finalGrid.data(), finalDev + nxy, nzl * planeBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n            MPI_Gatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, planeType, finalGrid.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(), planeType,\n                        0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        } else {\n            std::vector<Real> stage(nzl * nxy);\n            if (nzl > 0)\n                CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(stage.data(), finalDev + nxy, nzl * planeBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n            MPI_Gatherv(stage.data(), static_cast<int>(nzl), planeType, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, planeType, 0,\n                        MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        }\n\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            // Print results for external validation\n            if (printResults) print_results(finalGrid, \"Grid\");\n\n            // Validation\n            if (validate) {\n                printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n                bool valid = validateResult(finalGrid, nx, ny, nz);\n                if (valid) {\n                    printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n                } else {\n                    printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n                    rc = 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // --- Cleanup ---\n    if (d1) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d1));\n    if (d2) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d2));\n    if (hSendLo) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFreeHost(hSendLo));\n    if (hSendHi) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFreeHost(hSendHi));\n    if (hRecvLo) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFreeHost(hRecvLo));\n    if (hRecvHi) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFreeHost(hRecvHi));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamDestroy(sBnd));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamDestroy(sInt));\n    MPI_Type_free(&planeType);\n\n    return rc;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n    int rank = 0, size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    const int rc = runBenchmark(argc, argv, rank, size);\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return rc;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file
